keyFindings.description: A block id over the B-tree key limit (about 2.7 kB incompressible, e.g. a callout {#<3200 hex chars>}, which pmdoc accepts) makes every version write of that document fail: reproduced with a throwaway test on Postgres 17, NamedVersion at the head fails 'index row size 3232 exceeds btree version 4 maximum 2704 for index "document_blocks_pkey"' and stores no version; the same test on main 81a3b5ef stores version 1. The reconciler then retries the owed document forever.

Row key `${node.kind}:${node.id}:${kind}:${direction}` repeats when one source cites two blocks of the viewed document (refs/graph.go returns one edge per target block, edge.block differs): duplicate React keys among siblings, with per-row Excerpt state. Main keyed rows by kind:direction:created_at. Key must include edge.block; add the one-source-two-blocks case to ReferencedBy.test.tsx.

New refusal at the CLI/tool boundary without a '## Contract change census': on main dispatchRefFromUrl mapped a dashboard URL ending #b-<id> to its document, so comment/suggest/doc-edit/doc-read acted on the document; now the URL becomes a block ref and those tools refuse it. The PR body needs the census (search commands, hits with dispositions, rollout line).

Both files cross 1000 lines (routes.ts 910 -> 1027, references_test.go 662 -> 1549) with separable responsibilities: move block-reference parsing/formatting out of routes.ts and the block tests into a block-specific test file, as block_links_test.go already is.

parseBlockFragment turns any digit string into a JS number; Go's parseBlock refuses a pin past int64. A pin past 2^53 is rounded (and past 1e21 printed in exponent form) when the dashboard rebuilds the reference, so the dashboard links text the server does not treat as a reference and requests a different one. Bound the pin as Go does and add the overflow rows to the shared text-reference table.
